content:
Meta announces that parents can receive alerts via its artificial intelligence on Instagram, Facebook, or Meta Horizons when their children discuss suicide or other forms of self-harm.

You need to first register to use Meta's parental and guardian supervision tools before you can select the family accounts you wish to monitor……

Meta stated that this new feature is a supplement to existing safety measures.

The company said they hope to be able to detect even relatively subtle related content, but all flagged conversations will undergo manual review.

If you have not yet set up family supervision features for your child's account, you will need to do so first. This new feature is currently being rolled out in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia.

Meta currently notifies emergency services when it detects credible suicide risk in Facebook or Instagram posts, and stated that this measure will be extended to Meta AI in the future.

If you yourself feel at risk, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988, or have an online conversation at 988lifeline.org. You can also call 911 or go to the emergency room to request assistance with mental health emergencies.
